transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-11-02 16:00 PT | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Samir (AE), Nina (SE) - Redwood; Liam, Meera, Raj, Anika - Peregrine

Summary/Agenda (auto-gen): latency & throughput discovery; p95 targets; streaming and token/sec benchmarking; hosted vs dedicated constraints; security and VPC questions.

00:00 Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samir with Redwood, joined by Nina our SE. quick roundtable?
00:12 Liam: Liam O'Connor here, head of platform at Peregrine. we're evaluating inference infra for our customer-facing chat assistant.
00:20 Meera: Meera, ML eng working on model stack and benchmarks.
00:24 Raj: Raj, SRE. mainly worried about capacity planning and SLA.
00:28 Anika: Anika, product - interested in latency targets for user experience.
00:33 Samir: Great. high level, can you walk us through what you need for p95 and concurrency?
00:40 Liam: We're targeting p95 below 1.2s for single-turn streaming responses at our median prompt size (~150 tokens). concurrency wise we expect bursts to 200 concurrent users during peak and sustained 40-50 concurrency. token/sec is important because we're streaming incremental tokens to the UI.
01:05 Nina: ok, got it. when you say streaming, do you mean chunked token-by-token streaming to the browser? Any decoder constraints?
01:12 Meera: yes, token-by-token streaming. model is a 7B open model fine-tuned for our domain; we care about both latency and cost. need to understand tradeoffs between hosted and dedicated.
01:25 Samir: Cool. some clarifying Qs - what's the typical sequence length distribution and KV cache behavior? do you preserve chat context across calls?
01:33 Meera: average sequence ~512 tokens including history; we typically keep last 6 turns cached client-side but server side we want prefix caching so we don't re-encode everything each time. KV cache is important for repeated context across a session.
01:46 Raj: For SRE, important: we need predictable tail latency. p95 is fine but p99 is also important for some flows. Do you offer SLOs or SLAs on Dedicated?
01:58 Samir: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and performance targets; we can size pools and reserve capacity to meet SLOs. Hosted is best-effort but often enough for early experiments. for strict p95/p99 we typically recommend Dedicated or Private with pinned capacity.
02:15 Meera: How do you measure token/sec and what benchmark can we run to reproduce results?
02:21 Nina: We have a benchmark runner (we'll share) that measures token generation rate, warm/cold latency, streaming throughput, and concurrency scaling. It can run in your VPC or on a test dataset against our hosted endpoints.
02:36 Liam: curious about batching - we need low latency, how much batching would increase p95?
02:41 Nina: continuous batching tries to pack requests without adding too much latency; there's always a trade-off. with target p95 ~1.2s for 150 tokens we can configure small batch windows and prefix caching to hit that with Dedicated. quantization profiles can also reduce kernel time.
02:58 Raj: Security question - data residency and KMS. we need customer-managed keys and audit logs for every request.
03:04 Samir: For Private and Dedicated we support KMS integrations and detailed audit logs; we also have SOC 2 and can provide SAML/SSO with RBAC. we'll attach the security pack.
03:14 Anika: For UX - streaming jitter is noticeable if tokens arrive slowly; is there control over flush frequency?
03:20 Nina: yes, we expose stream chunking and buffer flush configs. you can tune flush size/time to get smoother UX versus raw token latency.
03:30 Meera: Are there fallback/degeneration strategies if capacity is overloaded?
03:34 Samir: We have smart routing and fallback to smaller model variants or different regions; Dedicated can burst to shared hosted capacity as a fallback. policies are configurable.
03:45 Liam: Cost -what's the price delta between hosted and reserved Dedicated?
03:50 Samir: Hosted is pay-as-you-go per token; Dedicated is a commitment with lower per-token effective cost and predictable throughput. we'll send a cost comparison.
03:58 Meera: For benchmarking, can we test with our model weights or do we need a proxy?
04:03 Nina: For Private deployments you can point to your weights; for hosted we can onboard compatible model artifacts or run a synthetic run with a near-equivalent open model. either way, we'll run token/sec and p95 measurements.
04:16 Raj: what's expected concurrency per GPU? we need sizing guidance so our infra team can provision network and autoscaling.
04:22 Nina: depends on model and quantization: for a quantized 7B on A100-like hardware you'd expect X tokens/sec per GPU; in practice we provide sizing recommendations - we'll run pilot benchmarks at 40/100/200 concurrent to produce exact numbers for your workload.
04:40 Liam: we want the raw numbers: p95 at 150 tokens, streaming, 40 sustained concurrency and 200 peak.
04:47 Samir: Agreed - that's what we'll measure. we'll run runs with warm KV cache vs cold to show delta.
04:55 Meera: can you include p99 too? We have flows where p99 matters.
05:00 Nina: yes, p99 and percent of requests hitting SLO buckets.
05:05 Anika: timeline - we need a pilot before EOY; is that feasible?
05:09 Samir: yes, we can aim to have benchmark results and a Dedicated sizing proposal within two weeks.
05:14 Liam: constraints - we must keep data in EU for some customers; EU region availability important.
05:19 Samir: Redwood has multi-region hosting; Dedicated private deployments can be in EU region or on-prem if needed.
05:25 Raj: will need a security review cycle; can you share SOC 2 docs and KMS integration guide?
05:30 Samir: yes, we'll attach SOC2, ISO blurb, and a KMS/HSM integration doc.
05:36 Meera: small nit - how does KV cache invalidation work across sessions?
05:40 Nina: there's TTL and explicit eviction APIs; for shared prefix caching we recommend session keys and TTL aligned with user session.
05:48 Liam: ok let's recap next steps.
05:52 Samir: Recap: Redwood to send benchmark runner and dataset, run initial benchmark against hosted endpoints (and Dedicated sizing runs if you provide test creds), send pricing and security pack, schedule infra+security follow-up. customers to provide concurrency profile, sample prompts, and decision timeline.
06:06 Liam: That works. thanks all.

Action items (as discussed):
- Samir: pricing + dedicated vs hosted comparison (by 2027-11-03)
- Nina: benchmark runner, sample dataset, and runbook + kickoff instructions (by 2027-11-03)
- Peregrine (Liam/Meera): share sample prompt corpus and expected concurrency profile (by 2027-11-04)

References/shared artifacts: link: https://redwood.internal/benchmarks/peregrine-2027 (SE will share runner); security pack: https://redwood.internal/security/peregrine-pack (placeholder link).

End of transcript.
